title: Canonical signed total tensor stalk comparison and chain naturality
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a commutative ring, and $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Use the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf], and the module-valued stalk $S(F)=F_{\bar t}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. For unbounded cochain complexes $C,D$ of $A_T$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], tensor means the direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], also for ordinary $A$-module complexes: degree $n$ is $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}C^p\otimes D^q$ and the differential on bidegree $(p,q)$ is $d_C\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_D$. There is a unique natural chain isomorphism
$$\theta_{C,D}:S(C\otimes_{A_T}D)\xrightarrow{\sim}SC\otimes_A SD$$
with the following normalization. If $p+q=n$, $\iota_{p,q}$ is the source total-complex coprojection, $\iota'_{p,q}$ the target coprojection, and $\gamma_{M,N}:S(M\otimes_{A_T}N)\to SM\otimes_A SN$ the ordinary tensor comparison for $A_T$-module sheaves $M,N$, characterized by $\gamma((s\otimes t)_{\bar t})=s_{\bar t}\otimes t_{\bar t}$ for sections on a common pointed etale neighbourhood, then
$$\theta_{C,D}^n\circ S(\iota_{p,q})=\iota'_{p,q}\circ\gamma_{C^p,D^q}.$$
For every pair of chain maps $f:C\to C'$, $g:D\to D'$ one has
$$\theta_{C',D'}\circ S(f\otimes g)=(Sf\otimes Sg)\circ\theta_{C,D}.$$
No boundedness or termwise flatness is required; totalization uses the countable coproducts indexed by $p+q=n$, not products.

proof.text:
First use the constant sections of $A_T$ to regard every $A_T$-module sheaf as a sheaf of $A$-modules. The two sheaf tensor products agree: an $A$-bilinear map of sheaves is $A_T$-balanced because a section of $A_T$ is locally constant, so the balancing equation reduces on a cover to balancing by an element of $A$ and then glues. This uses the sheafified tensor universal property, not equality of the sectionwise tensor products. Apply clause (1) of lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar with $\Lambda=A$ and invert its isomorphism. It gives precisely $\gamma_{M,N}:S(M\otimes_{A_T}N)\cong SM\otimes_A SN$, natural in both module sheaves, with the required formula on pure tensor germs. Thus for maps $u:M\to M'$ and $v:N\to N'$,
$\gamma_{M',N'}S(u\otimes v)=(Su\otimes Sv)\gamma_{M,N}$.
The coefficient action is the action of constant germs, so this is the stated $A$-linear comparison.

source.place: Tag 03EL, label lemma-tensor-product-pullback; sheaf tensor universal property immediately preceding it; geometric-point specialization

proof.text:
For a small family $(M_i)$, the module-sheaf colimit theorem identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of $\bigoplus_i M_i$ with the abelian-sheaf coproduct. Apply lem-kun-stalks-commute-colimits to this abelian diagram. Hence the canonical map
$k:\bigoplus_i SM_i\longrightarrow S(\bigoplus_i M_i)$, with $k j_i=S(\iota_i)$, is bijective on underlying abelian groups. Its maps are $A$-linear because each stalk map sends $a m_{\bar t}$ to $a(S\iota_i)(m_{\bar t})$; its inverse is therefore $A$-linear as well. Write $\alpha=k^{-1}$. This explicitly obtains module coproduct preservation from abelian coproduct preservation. Also $S(u+v)=Su+Sv$ and $S(-u)=-Su$: on a germ $m_{\bar t}$ both sides are respectively $(u(m)+v(m))_{\bar t}$ and $(-u(m))_{\bar t}$. Thus $S$ is additive and commutes with the signs used below.

proof.text:
For each $n$, put $I_n=\{(p,q)\in\mathbf Z^2:p+q=n\}$. Define
$\theta^n=(\bigoplus_{I_n}\gamma_{C^p,D^q})\alpha$.
It is an isomorphism: its inverse is the map $\bigoplus_{I_n}SC^p\otimes_A SD^q\to S(\bigoplus_{I_n}C^p\otimes_{A_T}D^q)$ whose restriction to summand $(p,q)$ is $S(\iota_{p,q})\gamma_{C^p,D^q}^{-1}$. The two composites restrict to the identity on every coproduct summand and hence are identities by the colimit universal property. By construction
$\theta^n S(\iota_{p,q})=\iota'_{p,q}\gamma_{C^p,D^q}$.
In particular the maps $S(\iota_{p,q})$ jointly determine maps out of the source degree, since $k$ in step 2 is an isomorphism.

proof.text:
For chain maps $f:C\to C'$ and $g:D\to D'$, the total tensor map restricts on bidegree $(p,q)$ to $f^p\otimes g^q$. Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\theta_{C',D'}^n S((f\otimes g)^n)S(\iota_{p,q})
&=\iota'_{C',D',p,q}\gamma_{C'^p,D'^q}S(f^p\otimes g^q)\\
&=\iota'_{C',D',p,q}(Sf^p\otimes Sg^q)\gamma_{C^p,D^q}\\
&=((Sf\otimes Sg)^n)\theta_{C,D}^n S(\iota_{p,q}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The middle equality is exactly step 1's simultaneous naturality. Joint determination gives equality in every degree, hence equality of chain maps. This proves naturality in both complexes with the specified normalization.

source.place: Tag 07A4, label lemma-pullback-tensor-product, bifunctoriality; expanded coprojection equation

proof.text: Any chain isomorphism with the displayed normalization has the same composite with every $S(\iota_{p,q})$ in each degree as $\theta$. Step 3 and the coproduct universal property force its degree maps, and consequently the chain map, to equal $\theta$. The construction uses only the small countable sets $I_n$ (each is indexed by $p\in\mathbf Z$ with $q=n-p$). Every differential sends one summand into just the two indicated summands. Thus all formulas define maps on direct sums even for unbounded complexes, and no flatness or boundedness was used.
